assertions.title: OAuth token refresh on 401 during `ft sync --api`

steps.action: Read xauth.ts source to verify refreshOAuthToken implementation
steps.expected: Function that calls X OAuth token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token, saves with mode 0600, and produces actionable error on expired refresh token
steps.observed: refreshOAuthToken() in src/xauth.ts: sends POST to https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token; on 401/invalid_request throws 'OAuth session expired. Re-run: ft auth'; saveTwitterOAuthToken() writes file with chmod 0o600

steps.action: Read bookmarks.ts source to verify automatic 401 retry with refresh
steps.expected: withTokenRefresh wrapper that intercepts 401, calls refreshOAuthToken, saves new token, and retries
steps.observed: withTokenRefresh() in src/bookmarks.ts: wraps API calls, detects status 401, calls refreshOAuthToken(), saves via saveTwitterOAuthToken(), retries once; also in syncTwitterBookmarks() pagination loop, 401 triggers refresh+retry with same pattern; both paths throw 'OAuth session expired. Re-run: ft auth' when refresh fails with expired token

steps.action: Run xauth unit tests (npx tsx --test tests/xauth.test.ts)
steps.expected: 3 tests pass: saveTwitterOAuthToken writes mode 0600; refreshOAuthToken returns new token pair on success; refreshOAuthToken throws on expired refresh token
steps.observed: All 3 tests pass: ✔ saveTwitterOAuthToken: writes private token file on posix ✔ refreshOAuthToken: returns new token pair on success ✔ refreshOAuthToken: throws on expired refresh token. Error message verified: 'OAuth session expired. Re-run: ft auth'

evidence.testResults: 3/3 pass in xauth.test.ts; 243/243 pass in full suite

assertions.issues: No dedicated unit test for withTokenRefresh() wrapper in bookmarks.ts. The refresh logic is tested via xauth.test.ts (refreshOAuthToken function) and the bookmarks.ts source code inspection confirms the integration. A dedicated test for the 401→refresh→retry flow in bookmarks.ts would strengthen coverage, but the underlying refresh function is verified.

assertions.title: Gap-fill state persists across interrupted runs

steps.action: Read graphql-bookmarks.ts source for syncGaps implementation
steps.expected: State file bookmarks-gapfill-state.json records processedIds; on re-run, already-processed IDs are skipped; progress indicates resumption
steps.observed: syncGaps() in src/graphql-bookmarks.ts loads state from twitterGapfillStatePath(), reads processedIds from GapfillState, filters allFetchIds to remove already-processed IDs, sets resumedFrom counter, and emits onProgress with done=resumedFrom indicating resumption. State is checkpointed every 100 fetches and on final save.

steps.action: Run graphql-bookmarks.test.ts — specifically syncGaps state persistence tests
steps.expected: Tests verify: state file created with processedIds; re-running skips already-processed IDs; progress starts from resumed count
steps.observed: ✔ syncGaps: saves processed IDs to bookmarks-gapfill-state.json (37.6ms) — verifies state file created with processedIds including the quotedStatusId. ✔ syncGaps: re-running skips already-processed IDs (10.3ms) — pre-populates state with processedIds=['555'], runs syncGaps, verifies only '666' is processed and progress starts at done>=1 for resumption.

steps.expected: ft sync --gaps is recognized and runs gap-fill mode
steps.observed: ft sync --help shows --gaps flag. Running ft sync --gaps with empty data dir outputs 'Filling gaps (quoted tweets, truncated text)...' and 'No gaps found — all bookmarks are fully enriched.' — no errors.

terminalSnapshots: ft sync --gaps with empty data dir: shows 'Filling gaps (quoted tweets, truncated text)...' then 'No gaps found — all bookmarks are fully enriched.' — exits 0
evidence.testResults: 2/2 syncGaps state persistence tests pass; 40/40 graphql-bookmarks.test.ts pass total

assertions.title: Corrupted gap-fill state file is handled gracefully

steps.action: Read graphql-bookmarks.ts syncGaps for corrupted state handling
steps.expected: When state file has invalid JSON, catch block logs warning and proceeds with complete pass
steps.observed: In syncGaps(), the state file read is wrapped in try/catch: if readJson throws (invalid JSON), the catch block executes console.warn('Gap-fill state file corrupted; starting fresh.') and sets processedIds = new Set(), allowing a complete pass from the beginning.

steps.action: Run graphql-bookmarks.test.ts — corrupted state file test
steps.expected: Test verifies corrupted state file produces warning and fresh start
steps.observed: ✔ syncGaps: corrupted state file produces warning and starts fresh (2.87ms) — writes truncated JSON '{"processedIds": [' to state file, runs syncGaps, verifies: (1) result.total===1 (processes the single ID from scratch), (2) warnings include message containing 'corrupted'. Test does not crash.

steps.action: Run full test suite to verify no regression

evidence.testResults: 1/1 corrupted state test pass; 40/40 graphql-bookmarks.test.ts pass; 243/243 full suite pass

assertions.issues: Minor: the warning uses 'corrupted' in the test assertion but the actual console.warn message says 'Gap-fill state file corrupted; starting fresh.' — test checks for substring 'corrupted' which matches. The source code catch block is a bare `catch {}` which catches all errors (including non-JSON errors), which is appropriate for this resilience pattern.
